title: Founders in Focus: Hagai Shapira of Daylight
summary: Meet Hagai Shapira, co-founder of Daylight, and learn how the Okta Ventures portfolio company combines AI and human expertise to transform security operations.
body_markdown:
Each month we highlight one of the founders of an[Okta Ventures](https://www.okta.com/company/okta-ventures/) portfolio company. You’ll learn more about them and how they work with Okta. This month, we’re speaking with Hagai Shapira of Daylight.


## What is Daylight and what is your mission?


[Daylight](https://daylight.ai/) is the security work company. We combine an AI-native security platform with expert security engineers to detect, investigate, and respond to cyberthreats. Our mission is to bring the scale of AI and the depth of human ingenuity to teams everywhere, empowering them to defend against the threats we know and those the world has yet to see.


## What were you doing prior to Daylight that led you to this moment?


My co-founder, Eldad Rudich, and I were working together at Torq. I was an early product leader, and Rudich was Torq’s first employee and VP of Research and Development.


We knew security services weren’t working the way customers needed them to and asked what they should become next. We saw the opportunity to rebuild the model entirely around what AI and humans each do best.


## What is Daylight’s solution? What challenge does it solve?


Security environments have expanded, threats have accelerated, and AI has fundamentally changed what attackers and defenders can do. Yet traditional managed security providers rely on human-heavy models that struggle to scale and offer little flexibility. At the same time, standalone AI tools add more complexity and operational burden to already stretched security teams.


Daylight introduces a new model for security operations, bringing together detection and response, threat hunting, AI security, and security data management through an AI-native platform and security engineering expertise.


Through Aura, our AI-native platform, AI agents and security engineers work within each customer's environment, continuously adapting to their systems, workflows, risks, and priorities. Agents handle day-to-day security operations, while engineers focus on complex investigations and decisions requiring human judgment. Customers can investigate threats using natural language, access security data in a centralized data lake, and manage their security operations from a single place.


Unlike traditional providers, Daylight doesn't force customers into a prescribed operating model. Organizations can choose fully managed, co-managed, or forward-deployed services depending on their team's capabilities and the level of control they want to retain.


The result is threat detection in seconds, response and containment in minutes, and up to 10 times faster operations than traditional managed security providers. Security teams gain access to AI at scale and exceptional human expertise without taking on more tools, headcount, or operational overhead.


## Why did Daylight want to work with Okta?


Identity is central to modern security operations, and Okta is one of the most widely adopted identity providers in the market. Okta was one of Daylight’s earliest integrations, giving our platform critical identity context to detect, investigate, and respond to threats. Building on that foundation, we see an opportunity to work more closely with the Okta team, deepen our technical integration, and deliver even greater value to our shared customers.


## How is Daylight working with Okta? What support do you look for in a corporate partner?


Okta Ventures invested in Daylight because we share a vision for how AI can transform security operations, with identity playing a critical role in understanding and responding to threats. In a corporate partner, we value deep technical expertise, opportunities for product collaboration, access to enterprise customers, and the ability to work together to solve real security challenges.


## What trends do you expect to see in the security industry?


Security teams are facing an unprecedented amount of noise as AI accelerates both the volume and sophistication of threats. The challenge is no longer just detecting suspicious activity, but determining what's real, what's not, and what actually requires action. Security teams will need more than another AI security operations tool or promises of automation. They'll need reliable answers, experienced security experts, and AI that can deliver real outcomes rather than marketing hype.
